body.statement: For every \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), the full-fiber Gaussian minimax regret equals \(L(r)\); the infimum over \(\delta\) is attained, \(L\) is continuous on \(\mathcal R_B\), and \(V^*=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B}L(r)\) is attained. The value also equals the supremum of finite-prior Bayes values over \(\mathcal H\).
body.justification: This identifies the design objective and establishes that both the terminal rule and annotation optimum exist.
body.gap: Masten and Kato analyze many-action games for treatment arms; the theorem concerns correlated overlapping policy values whose covariance is chosen through selective outcome observation.
body.consumer: Prospective validators obtain a well-defined population target \(V^*\) instead of a collection of unrelated contrast variances.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(r\in\mathcal R_B\). Positivity in \(\mathrm{lem:efficient\text{-}contrast\text{-}information}\) makes \(I_r\) and \(\Sigma(r)\) positive definite. Consider the Gaussian cell-mean experiment \(Y_G\sim N(b,I_r^{-1})\) with nuisance fiber \(A_{\mathrm{map}}b=h\). The statistic \(Z=A_{\mathrm{map}}Y_G\) has law \(N(h,\Sigma(r))\), so rules based on \(Z\) prove that the full-fiber value is at most \(L(r)\). On the least-favourable slice \(b=T_rh\), define \(E_G=Y_G-T_rA_{\mathrm{map}}Y_G\). The information identities imply
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(E_G,Z)=I_r^{-1}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top-T_r\Sigma(r)=0,
\qquad E(E_G)=T_rh-T_rh=0.
\]
Joint Gaussianity makes \(E_G\) independent of \(Z\), and its law is independent of \(h\). Hence it is ancillary on this slice and cannot lower the minimax regret below the \(Z\)-game. The reverse inequality follows, proving equality with \(L(r)\).

For existence, let \(\mu\) be any Gaussian probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue measure and represent a rule as \((\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_M)\in L^\infty(\mu)^M\) with nonnegative coordinates summing to one. This set is weak-star compact by \(\mathrm{lem:weak\text{-}star\text{-}rule\text{-}compactness}\), and each risk is weak-star continuous because the corresponding normal density times the bounded regret belongs to \(L^1(\mu)\). The set of probability measures on compact \(\mathcal H\) is compact and convex. Applying \(\mathrm{lem:sion\text{-}minimax}\) to rule and prior yields a minimax rule and equality of the minimax value with the supremum of Bayes values over all priors.

Let \(U=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\) and \(R_0=2U\). Compactness of \(\mathcal R_B\), positivity of \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\), and full row rank give constants \(0<\lambda_0\le\lambda_{\min}\{\Sigma(r)\}\) for all \(r\). For densities \(p,q\), partitioning over \(\{p\ge q\}\), applying the log-sum inequality on the two partition cells, and differentiating the resulting Bernoulli divergence gives \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q)^2\le D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P,Q)/2\). Applying this proved scalar inequality to equal-covariance normals and using the two-Lipschitz property of regret gives
\[
|R_r(h,\delta)-R_r(g,\delta)|
\le\left(2+\frac{R_0\sqrt d}{2\sqrt{\lambda_0}}\right)\lVert h-g\rVert_\infty.
\]
Therefore finitely supported priors are weakly dense without changing Bayes values by more than the right-hand modulus, proving that their supremum already equals \(L(r)\).

Finally, \(r\mapsto\Sigma(r)\) is continuous on \([\rho,1]^{2K}\). The Gaussian covariance formula and the entropy-to-total-variation inequality above imply uniform total-variation continuity over \(h\in\mathcal H\); taking infima and suprema preserves this modulus, so \(L\) is continuous. The set \(\mathcal R_B\) is nonempty, closed, and bounded, hence compact. Every minimizing sequence has a convergent subsequence in \(\mathcal R_B\), and continuity makes its limit attain \(V^*\).
